cases.reason: Unlike a bare map gap, Physical has a coherent body of already-discovered domain-specific residual pressure that World explicitly refuses to own as domain mechanism. This is sufficient to justify a separate proposal review, not to establish a project or owner.
cases.scopeCandidate: Physical reality / domain-specific physical mechanisms as a research programme, initially bounded by the coherent World residual/falsifier corpus rather than the full Physical & Material navigation region.

cases.reason: The navigation region combines cosmology/spacetime, Earth-system sciences and cross-region agriculture. MajorRegion coherence is insufficient evidence of project coherence.
cases.scopeCandidate: Entire 14-member MajorRegion as one research programme.
cases.target: Earth, Planetary & Space Systems as one project

cases.reason: World already identifies a coherent unexplored continent and owner boundary. This is enough for proposal review eligibility, not enough for owner admission.
cases.scopeCandidate: Relativity/spacetime/cosmology frontier explicitly identified but unworked by World.

cases.reason: The bounded scan found no dedicated current programme, but Atlas does not yet have a coherent residual corpus or tested owner-boundary matrix sufficient to propose a programme. A scoping survey should precede project proposal review.

findings.claim: Owner-gap evidence does not map one-to-one to project proposals: Physical is proposal-review eligible, the whole Earth/Space region is not, cosmology/spacetime is separately eligible, and Earth-system sciences require scoping first.
MajorRegion boundaries are navigation projections and may be too broad or heterogeneous to serve as project boundaries.
Project proposal review can be justified by either coherent residual evidence or a coherent known-unworked frontier, but neither route establishes semantic owner admission.

The strongest next Atlas contribution is routing quality: preserving evidence and owner-boundary constraints while delegating actual charter/admission decisions to the Research System rather than expanding Atlas authority.
